context:
Reuse dev_loop_pr_metrics.py, event_fanout_v1, current GitHub pagination and its tests. Freeze cohort/time window and PR/head/base/run/attempt identifiers before aggregation; fetch bounded projected data and cache read-only evidence by immutable identity. Enumerate all synchronize heads and every attempt, then separately correlate speculative merge_group and post-merge runs. Generate report numbers and validation from the same data, not selected manual sums. This item changes measurement code only, not CI routing, queue settings or gate coverage.

Extend this collector's existing validation machinery with --validate-lifecycle-baseline PATH --process-baseline PATH and --validate-refresh-audit PATH --baseline PATH. The first validates immutable identity completeness, all-head/run-attempt totals, explicit missingness and the preregistered process criteria. Include refresh observations keyed by PR/head/run/attempt with verdict/reason, or explicit missing-artifact status. The second reads a machine-readable JSON block embedded in the exact-refresh Markdown audit and recomputes its reason-code counts, denominator, missingness and timing-only share from that shared baseline; reject omitted/duplicate identities, changed windows, unknown denominators and conflated prior_check_not_success/prior_check_unbound. Unit tests include tampered totals, omitted superseded heads and changed thresholds. These are local report validators, not new CI gates or an additional sampler.
description:
Extend the original representative 28-day per-PR remeasurement, rather than create another metrics framework. The existing event_fanout_for_pr collector queries only the final merged head; it cannot establish total refresh/cancellation cost. Repair that coverage first, then produce the complete representative cohort and baseline for pr-process-low-drama-acceptance. Retain existing metric meanings and label new fields/version explicitly. Evidence: _project/scripts/dev_loop_pr_metrics.py:388-402; #2076/#2077 report corrections; session 01a07292. The 28-day historical sample may include incomplete/expired evidence, which must be quantified as missing rather than silently excluded.

PREREGISTRATION OWNER: w0 also freezes _project/analysis/pr-process-acceptance-baseline.json BEFORE any dependent implementation begins. Record the source session, incident scenarios, metric definitions, historical cohort/window, exclusions and missing evidence, safety and efficiency thresholds, prospective strata and minimum 10-PR/7-day observation, registration timestamp and baseline commit. Register the 50% avoidable-action reduction target before observing implementation results. This is immediate historical/planning work, not a prerequisite seven-day prospective wait. Final acceptance only consumes and validates this frozen record. Any later criteria change is versioned and disclosed, never silently applied to a measured cohort.

FEATURE-BATCH PREREGISTRATION: w0 must define delivery IDs, member counts/scopes, first work/commit/prepare/integration/PR-open/merge timestamps, feature-mode strata and comparison units before this new mode is implemented. Measure full feature-start-to-land lead time, agent/user effort, local and hosted validation across worker and integration branches, cancelled/abandoned work and backlog delivery throughput. Keep per-PR metrics for compatibility, but fewer PRs or a shorter post-open interval is not itself a saving. Compare equivalent delivered outcomes and change mix; apply the 50% avoidable-action target using the frozen comparable denominator, not a post-hoc per-PR denominator. Missing local history remains explicit. The existing 10-PR/7-day acceptance cohort includes feature batches without counting each member as a separate PR.

preserves.behavior: Missing evidence and censored observations remain explicit; changing the cohort requires a new snapshot.
No workflow skips, required-check changes, custom metrics framework or fabricated savings.
